title: Horizontal-gauge Mirror task codes
hypothesis: On held-out tasks with the same frozen attention backbone, a gauge-horizontal Mirror code reaches no worse than +0.01 nats/token relative to the best byte-matched ordinary task code, while reducing serialized code-bank bytes by at least 10% and not increasing P95 forward latency by over 10%.
physical_object: shared frozen attention Q/K/V/O maps and a source-task residual basis
mirror_coordinate: small task m in the numerically estimated horizontal (non-gauge) complement
logical_multiplicity: multiple genuinely different task attention functions from shared maps
closest_controls: unprojected Mirror code / direct low-rank code / native gauge-invariant optimization

requirements.native: Freeze a 2-head 32-wide attention block. Fit a regular shared task residual basis with unrestricted small task codes; separately instantiate unconstrained low-rank and rank-one codes. Preserve identical task split, optimizer and shared basis.
requirements.insertion: Compute attention-layer gauge tangent directions on the SOURCE models only (Q/K inverse coordinate transforms and V/O inverse output transforms). QR-project candidate low-dimensional residual directions away from these tangent directions. Train the remaining coefficients m from allowed per-task support examples. A projection or decomposition used at inference is paid in bytes/FLOPs unless compiled into the shared basis.
requirements.method: For each source model, sample invertible G for Q'=QG and K'=KG^{-T}, plus H for V'=VH and output map O'=H^{-1}O. Confirm attention/model outputs unchanged before estimating a gauge tangent. Construct finite-difference tangent columns and orthonormalize in float64. Compare m-basis before/after removing their tangent components; train 4 code sizes {2,4,8,16} and retain best dev. Do not assume a Frobenius-horizontal direction automatically gives lower end-to-end loss.
requirements.fixture: Synthetic teacher attention: d_model=32, heads=2, sequence=16; eight train/source tasks and four task-identity heldouts, each with disjoint support/dev/audit examples. A teacher generates coherent classification/next-token labels; no target oracle weight deltas allowed for fitting m. Repeat with random and structured task families.
requirements.hardware: Stage 1 CPU PyTorch float64 for gauge diagnostics, float32 for training; no GPU required. Stage 2 single CUDA GPU if available, otherwise record Stage-2 BLOCKED instead of inventing language-model results.

development.allowed: select code dimension, LR, stop condition only

resources.compute: training examples and updates, FLOPs or MACs, CPU/GPU P50/P95 with batch/dtype/hardware
resources.quality: Teacher/logit MSE, held-out cross entropy, output Jacobian singular-rank diagnostic on fixed probe inputs, per-task accuracy, serial bytes including QR/basis metadata, training FLOPs, CPU/GPU P50/P95 inference.

gates.PASS: All five fresh task-world seeds satisfy non-inferiority margin 0.01 nats/token vs best byte-near non-Mirror code, median additional serialized bytes <=0.90 control, median P95 <=1.10 control, and functional Jacobian rank is nonzero for each claimed logical role.
gates.FAIL: Any exact gauge transform is counted as a distinct logical function; or matched control reaches quality with <= candidate bytes and latency; or fresh quality margin is exceeded in >=2 of 5 worlds.
gates.UNCERTAIN: Missing strong control, uncertain precision, insufficient heldout data, unmeasured runtime or CI overlap

alternative: Gauge complement can rotate with task/data and a training-friendly horizontal projection can discard useful nonlinear directions; simpler low-rank basis may win.
uncertainty: Finite-probe tangent nullspace, near-degenerate rank, learned basis randomness, optimizer choice, float32 vs float64. Treat near-zero singular values as uncertain; bootstrap by task identity and report u_c from seeds plus numerical precision.
stopping: Stop after 3 dev seeds then 5 fresh worlds; if cheap mechanism fails predeclared gate, record negative and do not tune fresh. Hardware unavailable => BLOCKED (not PASS).
prior_art_delta: Test whether allocating m only to observable function directions improves capacity-per-byte beyond unconstrained codes; do not treat gauge orbit as a new expert.
limitations: A local/probe-space gauge complement is not a proof of global quotient geometry or independent expert capacity.
